title: Washing Machine Maintenance: Leveling, Hoses, and Leak-Prevention Upgrades
summary: This Old House demonstrates practical care and upgrades to reduce vibration, water leakage risk, and downtime for residential washing machines. The hosts begin by stressing that the unit should be level to minimize noise and movement during fast spinning, showing leveling legs and using a front-mounted level. They then discuss the water-supply side, noting back-wall hose connections, potential inline filters, and the risk of downstream shutoffs failing and clogging the inlet. The video contrasts rubber hoses with stainless steel braided hoses, explaining the higher durability of the latter and their lower burst risk. It surveys several leak-prevention approaches—manual and electronic shutoffs, and a floor-leak sensor—and explains a mechanical, non-electronic lever option that temporarily pressurizes the hoses for a limited window (two-and-a-half hours) and defaults to off, highlighting tradeoffs between simplicity and safety. The overall message is to combine proper leveling with robust hose fittings and reliable shut-off strategies to extend appliance life and reduce flood risk.
